claims.text: The additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has a homogeneous FCC matrix.
The starting alloy has high strength.
The starting alloy has notable fatigue resistance.
Under oxidizing conditions, selective oxidation forms a protective, coherent surface oxide scale.
Under reducing conditions, the protective scale is disrupted or fails to form completely.
Scale disruption under reducing conditions exposes the FCC matrix to accelerated degradation.
Elevated-temperature gas exposure does not cause significant phase transformation of the FCC matrix.
The protective surface scale is enriched in chromium and titanium oxides.
The chromium- and titanium-rich oxide scale acts as a barrier to further oxidation or internal degradation.
Chromium and titanium are minor alloying elements in the stated alloy.
Chromium and titanium preferentially oxidize under oxidizing conditions.
Preferential chromium and titanium oxidation produces a dense, coherent, self-healing scale.
Insufficient oxidation in a reducing atmosphere makes the surface scale incomplete or porous.
An incomplete or porous scale causes more rapid degradation despite phase stability of the alloy.
Oxidizing exposure will produce a continuous, adherent oxide layer that lowers the degradation rate and preserves mechanical properties.
Reducing exposure will produce a discontinuous or porous oxide layer accompanied by greater weight loss or microstructural damage.
Reducing exposure may embrittle the alloy.
The proposed mechanism applies approximately from 700 to 900 degrees Celsius.
Different processing-induced microstructures may change the proposed degradation behavior.

contradictions.description: The mechanism calls both Cr and Ti minor alloying elements, but the stated formula contains about 18.2 at.% Cr, making the characterization of Cr as minor inconsistent with the composition.
